Standard: Design usage, duty cycles addressing all sources of repeated loads, and environmental exposure applicable to the type design being certified are defined and validated. All source material (e.g., military specifications, contract requirements, program documents) is identified, and any modification of source material for the type design being certified is substantiated. Design usage definitions and environments include the following: a. Mission definition and percent utilization. b. Engine usage statistics (e.g., EFH, engine mission hours, engine operating time, throttle cycles, time at high power, dwell time, augmentor lights and time). c. Time at flight envelope extremities (e.g., 10 hours at any point in envelope). d. Thrust vectoring usage. e. Engine operating envelope. f. Engine attitude limits and exposure times. g. Ambient temperature distributions and percent utilization. h. Engine extractions and extraction duty cycle (e.g., bleed air, loaded accessory pads, PTO pads). i. Engine deterioration characteristics and percent utilization (e.g., 1/3 new, 2/3 fully deteriorated). j. Externally-applied forces (g’s, rotational rates and accelerations). k. Installed temperature, pressure, and vibration environment. l. Acoustic noise environment (installed and uninstalled). m. Icing environment. n. Sand and dust environment. o. Corrosion environment. p. Non-operating and transportation environment. q. Windmilling envelope. r. Cross-wind envelope. s. Electromagnetic environment. The damage content of simplified or composite duty cycles defined for analysis and test are shown to be equivalent to, or more severe than, that of the full mission usage set. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine design documentation or other source material to verify that all design usage, duty cycles, and environments necessary for the type design being certified are defined and valid. Sources are cited and modification of any source material is substantiated. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis defines usage and duty cycles for design, analysis, and test. Damage equivalency of resultant duty cycles is substantiated.
